grades.answer: The board scored like the backtest on NFL 2026's complete weeks 1–3 (League of Scrubs scoring, players who played), next to the walk-forward backtest (2021–2025). Week 4 is still being played; it counts once its last game is in.
howto: **Order score** (Spearman): how well the projected order of players matched the order they really finished in, 1 = perfect, 0 = no better than random. Around 0.5–0.6 is good for one week of fantasy football.
**Average miss** (MAE): how many points the projection missed by, on average, per player per game.
**Inside the range** (coverage): how often the real score landed between the floor and the ceiling. The aim is 8 weeks in 10.

**This season** scores the weeks already played on the board as it stood before kickoff; **backtest** is the same score on 2021 to 2025, each season predicted by a model trained only on the seasons before it. A few weeks are a small sample: one odd Sunday moves them a lot.

body.title: How to read this site's numbers
body.summary: What a projection and its range mean, how our record is kept before kickoff, and where the model has been wrong so far this season.
body.author: isuckatfantasy
body.markdown:
Every number on this site is one of three things: a **projection** (what we expect a player to score), a **range**
(how far from that he could land) or a **record** (how those calls turned out). This post says what each one means,
how we check it, and where it has gone wrong.

## A projection is the middle, not a promise

**Projected points this week** is the average of the weeks a player like him, in his role, against this defense,
usually has — priced in the scoring you picked (Half PPR unless you open your league, and then your league's own
rules, bonus by bonus). We project the stat line first (targets, catches, yards, touchdowns, carries, passes) and
price it second, so the same projection reads differently in PPR and in Standard.

A projection of 14.2 does not mean "he will score 14". It means 14 is the middle of what usually happens.

## The range is the honest part

Beside most projections you will see a range:

- **Low-end / high-end outcome**: 1 week in 10 he lands below the low end, 1 in 10 above the high end. So 8 weeks in
  10 land inside it.
- **Typical range**: the middle half of outcomes. Half his weeks land inside it.

These ranges are wide on purpose. For a top-24 wide receiver in Half PPR the low-end to high-end span is about 17
points, and the typical range about 9. That is what a fantasy week is like; a narrower range would only look more
confident.

We check that the ranges mean what they say. Over three past seasons (2023–2025, every week, played games only):

| Position | Inside the typical range (aim 50%) | Inside low-end to high-end (aim 80%) |
|---|---|---|
| RB | 51.3% | about 80% |
| WR | 49.6% | about 80% |
| TE | 50.7% | about 80% |
| QB | 47.2% | 75.8% |

> Quarterbacks fall below the low end too often: about 15 weeks in 100 instead of 10. Almost all of those are games
> he did not finish (an injury, a benching). The model cannot see those coming, and we have not fixed it.

## How the record is kept

Every week, before the first kickoff, we save two boards side by side: **our projections and Sleeper's own**. After
the last game we score both against what happened, in the same scoring:

1. **Start/sit calls**: for each lineup, the closest calls between two players. Whose numbers picked the one who
   scored more?
2. **The order**: did the players we ranked higher score more?
3. **The miss**: the average distance between the projection and the points, per player.

Nothing is filled in after the fact. A week that was not saved before kickoff is not on the record, so the record
starts with the first week both boards were saved. It is kept in Half PPR, the scoring of the league we project every
morning. **About the numbers** shows it week by week, including the weeks we lost.

## Where we have been wrong

Through the first three complete weeks of 2026, against the same model's numbers on 2021–2025:

- **Quarterbacks are the weak spot.** The order of our quarterback projections matched the results much less well than
  in past seasons (0.39 this season against 0.59 before, where 1 is a perfect order and 0 is no better than a guess),
  and the average miss was 6.5 points against 5.4.
- **Running backs and wide receivers are on their usual form**: an average miss of 4.2 points per player for both,
  close to past seasons.
- **Tight ends miss a little more than usual**: 3.5 points against 3.0.
- **We sit a little below the market.** Our numbers for the top 24 players run about 1 to 3 points under Sleeper's
  at most positions. Part of that is a real difference of opinion; part is that the fringe players get a little too
  much. Read the gap as "we are a bit more cautious", not as a fade.
- **Our lineups' early record is small and unflattering**: on the first two rebuilt weeks of our own league, the
  lineups we would have set scored about 1.2 points less per team per week than the ones the managers set. Two weeks
  is far too few to judge, and the real record starts with lineups saved before kickoff.

## What none of these numbers know

A projection counts a player's role, his offense, the defense he faces and the betting lines. It does not know who
will be inactive on Sunday morning until the injury report says so, it does not know that a coach has decided to
change the plan, and a matchup note (a shutdown cornerback, a defense that has struggled) is context we show beside
the number, not something added to it.

If a number here looks wrong to you, it might be. Open the player and read **Why this number**: every projection
says what it is built from.

Fumbles stay in the total, not in the rushing part. Signed: above 100% when his passing points are below zero (interceptions).
catalogue.aggregation: summed numerator / summed denominator over the window
catalogue.source: this league's scoring over nflverse weekly player stats

catalogue.definition: How far past the line of scrimmage his targets travel, on average (air yards per target).
catalogue.aggregation: summed numerator / summed denominator over the window
catalogue.reason: no targets

catalogue.label: Air-yard share
catalogue.definition: His receiving air yards / his team's passing air yards in the games he played. Signed: can be negative or pass 100% when the team's total is small.
catalogue.denominator: team passing air yards in the games he played
catalogue.aggregation: summed numerator / summed denominator over the games he played in the window (never a mean of weekly %)
catalogue.reason: his team's air yards in his games are zero

catalogue.label: Weighted opportunity rating (WOPR)
catalogue.definition: 1.5 × target share + 0.7 × air-yard share, both over the window (each summed numerator / summed denominator first). Weighs how much of his team's passing he draws, deep looks counting more.
catalogue.aggregation: the window's two shares, then combined
catalogue.reason: no team targets or air yards in his games

catalogue.label: Receiver air conversion ratio (RACR)
catalogue.definition: Receiving yards per air yard thrown his way: above 1 he gains more than the throws' depth (yards after the catch), below 1 less (incompletions, deep misses).
catalogue.aggregation: summed numerator / summed denominator over the window
catalogue.reason: his air yards in the window are zero or negative, so the ratio means nothing

catalogue.definition: nflfastR's completion percentage over expected, in points of percentage. Aggregated as the mean of his per-game CPOE weighted by pass attempts (nflverse publishes the per-game mean, not the per-throw sum): close to the per-throw mean, not identical. Not Next Gen Stats' CPOE.
catalogue.aggregation: attempt-weighted mean of per-game CPOE
catalogue.reason: no pass attempts with a CPOE

catalogue.label: Expected fantasy points
catalogue.definition: What his targets and carries were worth on average (an opportunity-based estimate of past games, not next week's projection), in this league's scoring, added up over his games with an expected value.
catalogue.aggregation: summed over his game rows in the window
catalogue.reason: no expected value for his games (a kicker, or games before the opportunity model)

catalogue.label: Expected fantasy points per game
catalogue.definition: What his targets and carries were worth on average (an opportunity-based estimate of past games, not next week's projection), in this league's scoring.
catalogue.aggregation: summed numerator / summed denominator over the window
catalogue.reason: no expected value for his games (a kicker, or games before the opportunity model)

catalogue.label: Points over expected
catalogue.definition: His fantasy points minus his expected fantasy points, over the same games (the games he played with an expected value), in this league's scoring. Positive: he scored more than his opportunities usually bring.
catalogue.numerator: fantasy points − expected points, same games
catalogue.aggregation: summed over the games with an expected value; per game divides by those games
catalogue.reason: no expected value for his games (a kicker, or games before the opportunity model)

catalogue.label: Average separation (yards)
catalogue.definition: NFL Next Gen Stats' average distance, in yards, between him and the nearest defender when the pass arrives (a catch or an incompletion), per target. A context number, not a talent score. NGS publishes a week only for a receiver or tight end with 5+ targets; over several weeks it is the mean of his weekly values weighted by NGS's targets — never a mean of means.
catalogue.denominator: NGS targets in his qualifying weeks
catalogue.aggregation: mean of NGS's weekly values weighted by the denominator NGS states, over his weeks in the window that NGS published (never a mean of means)

catalogue.reason: No Next Gen Stats week in this window: NGS publishes a week only when he clears its minimum (5+ targets, receivers and tight ends only), so this is unknown, not zero.

NGS publishes a week only for a receiver or tight end with 5+ targets; over several weeks it is the mean of his weekly values weighted by NGS's targets — never a mean of means.

catalogue.aggregation: mean of NGS's weekly values weighted by the denominator NGS states, over his weeks in the window that NGS published (never a mean of means)

catalogue.reason: No Next Gen Stats week in this window: NGS publishes a week only when he clears its minimum (5+ targets, receivers and tight ends only), so this is unknown, not zero.

catalogue.label: Intended air yards per target (Next Gen Stats)
catalogue.definition: NFL Next Gen Stats' average distance the ball was thrown past the line of scrimmage on his targets (tracking, so catchable and uncatchable throws alike). NGS publishes a week only for a receiver or tight end with 5+ targets; over several weeks it is the mean of his weekly values weighted by NGS's targets — never a mean of means.

catalogue.definition: NFL Next Gen Stats' yards after the catch minus what its tracking model expected at the catch, per reception. NGS publishes a week only for a receiver or tight end with 5+ targets; over several weeks it is the mean of his weekly values weighted by NGS's receptions — never a mean of means.
catalogue.numerator: weekly YAC over expected x NGS receptions
catalogue.denominator: NGS receptions in his qualifying weeks

catalogue.label: First-read target share
catalogue.definition: Of his team's charted targets thrown to the quarterback's first read, the share thrown to him — in the charted games he played. Built from charted targeted plays: it does not know every play's first-read assignment, only where the ball went when the first read was thrown to.

catalogue.denominator: team charted first-read targets in the charted games he played

catalogue.definition: Charted targets FTN marks catchable / his charted targets.
catalogue.aggregation: summed numerator / summed denominator over the window
catalogue.reason: FTN charting starts in 2022 and covers only the games charted so far this season.

catalogue.label: Charted targets
catalogue.definition: His targets on plays FTN charted (the sample behind first-read share and catchable rate).
catalogue.aggregation: summed over his game rows in the window
catalogue.reason: FTN charting starts in 2022 and covers only the games charted so far this season.

catalogue.label: Pressure splits
catalogue.definition: Results under pressure. Needs a licensed charting feed (PFF / FTN pressure); not available.

catalogue.label: Snap share
catalogue.definition: His share of his team's offensive snaps. nflverse publishes each game's share (rounded to the percent), not the team's snap total, so several games are the mean of his per-game shares over games with snap counts (each game weighted equally) — the card's Snap share.
catalogue.aggregation: mean of per-game snap share over games with snap counts
catalogue.reason: no snap counts recorded for his games

body.howto:
- **One row per player over the window you pick**: the season, his last 3 or 5 *games played*, the last 3 or 5 *calendar weeks* (a bye or a missed game leaves fewer games: **G** says how many), or a week range.
- **Per game** divides the window's total by the games he played in it; shares and rates keep their own denominators (target share = his targets / his team's targets in the games he played).
- A share over several games is the summed numerator over the summed denominator, never an average of weekly percentages.
- A dash means the number cannot be worked out here (no targets, a season without charting, routes in season); hover it for the reason. Never zero.
